item.title: Art && Code: Weird Reality
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Lead Technical Producer

WEIRD REALITY: A Conference for Emerging Immersive Media — New and Independent Visions for VR, AR, and MR. Hosted by the Frank-Ratchye Studio for Creative Inquiry at Carnegie Mellon University. Curated by Golan Levin.

I was responsible for producing and executing a public Virtual Reality exhibition featuring 18 installations and projects from artists working with VR. The exhibition took place in the Ballroom of the Ace Hotel, Pittsburgh, 2016.

item.title: AVATAR_AR: Co-Creation Project & Innovation in Documentary Media Course
item.description:
Overview

A digital storytelling project utilizing co-creation methodologies and a design-justice lens to create short web-first documentary stories made collaboratively with people in recovery from addiction, working to mitigate stigma on individual, institutional, and societal levels.

The Course

Innovation Studio in Documentary Media is an interdisciplinary course co-developed and taught by Anna Henson, Assistant Professor of Emerging Media Arts, and Dr. Dennis McChargue, Professor of Clinical Psychology at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. The course brought together clinical psychology, documentary storytelling, design justice and co-creation frameworks, and hands-on technical training in motion capture, avatar animation, and game engine production in Unreal Engine. The documentary project produced through the course is called AVATAR_AR (Addiction Recovery).

item.title: Big Fish: Musical Production & Projection Design Course
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Assistant Professor of Emerging Media Arts · Projection Designer · Course Developer

Big Fish is a Broadway musical about a son reconciling with his larger-than-life father’s tall tales.

This production marked the first time UNL students designed and executed projection design for a mainstage production — a full-scale collaboration between the Johnny Carson School of Theater and Film, the Johnny Carson Center for Emerging Media Arts, and the Glenn Korff School of Music, directed by Professor Ann Marie Pollard.

item.title: Body, My Body: Embodied VR
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Artist, Creative Technologist, Director

A continuation of the collaboration between slowdanger and Anna Henson, this project explores embodiment, touch, and proprioception through a participatory VR experience for one guest and two dancers, whose real-time tracked movements are reflected in the visual and auditory environment in-headset.

The virtual environment begins in darkness, a response to VR as a physical blindfold to the outside world. As the dancers move and interact with the participant, their abstract avatars illuminate the virtual architecture of the space, acting as flashlights and pathfinders for the person in headset. Though the headset is a physical barrier between the co-located participants in this experience, and the virtual avatars do not appear human, an intimate and synchronous interaction is still possible. This project engages the complex issue of trust within the liminal space between virtual and physical environments, specifically drawing attention to the persistence and implication of the physical world and co-present people within it.

item.title: Body, My Body: Music Video & Animation Research
item.description:
Overview

‘Body, My Body,’ is a music video made in collaboration with award-winning movement and music duo slowdanger, using volumetric capture and marker-based motion capture rigged to photogrammetry scans of the dancers’ bodies. Resulting point clouds were rendered through a custom app built with OpenFrameworks.

‘Body, My Body’ explores the continuum of human representation between photo-real and avatar, and the fragmented nature of a digital ‘self.’

item.title: Cello Quartet: Trimpin
item.description:
Overview

Cello Quartet features three autonomous cellos and a piano on moving platforms roaming the stage, playing in coordination with live cellist Lori Goldston and circus artists Joel Herzfeld, Bri Crabtree, and Calvin Kai Ku, choreographed by Margaret Fisher. Trimpin’s MIDI-controlled instruments — including a lampshade drum machine — draw on the influence of Henry Brant and Bauhaus artist Oskar Schlemmer’s Triadisches Ballett, with costumes by Cynthia DuVal.

Projection design by Anna Henson incorporates animations created computationally in collaboration with Dimitri Diakopoulos, using algorithms that map the sound frequencies of Trimpin’s music to corresponding colors in the light spectrum, alongside filmed footage of the cello instruments animated using custom AI tooling.

item.title: far field
item.description:
Overview

COLLABORATORS: Anna Henson and slowdanger · Assistant: Maricel Reinhard · Character Design: H. D. Harris · Engineer: Dimitri Diakopoulos

far field is a collaborative web-XR and VR experience that transforms pandemic-era Zoom interactions and personal recordings into an embodied virtual archive, exploring distance, perception, and fragmented presence across shared digital space.

Created during a period of enforced physical separation, the work draws on recorded movement, voice, and image gathered through remote collaboration to construct a virtual environment where those traces of presence can be re-inhabited and encountered anew. The piece investigates how affect and embodied experience persist — and change — when mediated through networked technologies.

item.title: Glass Inward
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Artist, Director, Projection Designer, Interface Designer

The Glass Inward awakens Orlando at the intersection of male and female, past and present, and the body and technology. Within this shifting environment, Orlando navigates relationships to others, time, and memory as the live body extends into cinematic, auditory, and coded doubles, foregrounding agency, surveillance, and identity in digitally entangled life. The work investigates the interplay between cinematic content, audience–actor interaction, and the splitting of character across physical and technological forms through custom storytelling interfaces (TouchOSC, Isadora, Ableton, Arduino), which performers manipulate in real time, controlling video, lighting, and amplified voice while under continuous webcam surveillance.

item.title: HBO / The Mill: Lovecraft Sanctum VR
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Social VR Designer and VR Experience Guide

A storytelling experience that brought the works of James Baldwin, Sonia Sanchez and Janelle Monae to VR. A series of exclusive virtual reality events, which transported fans into a world inspired by the hit HBO show, Lovecraft Country. SanctumVR was custom built inside of VRChat, a social VR platform, and allowed guests to inhabit avatars, and see and interact with other guests in real time within the immersive environment, as well as complete puzzles and interactive experiences inspired by the TV show. Guests explored the world, shepherded by a live VR Guide, and experienced three live events throughout the season with guest voiceover performances by Jurnee Smollett, Jonathan Majors, Courtney B. Vance, and Michael Kenneth Williams. Users who weren’t able to participate within the social VR space could watch the livestream on YouTube and also interact in real-time, solving riddles to trigger spells that directly impacted the experience.

item.title: Molt: MIX NYC
item.description:
Overview

ARTISTS: Anna Henson and Shawn Escarciga

Molt is an immersive video installation created in collaboration with Shawn Escarciga, presented at MIX NYC 2015: The New York Queer Experimental Film Festival. Drawing on the biological metaphor of molting — the violent and tender process by which a creature sheds its former self to become something new — the work uses layered video projection and spatial sound to create an environment of transformation, vulnerability, and emergence.

item.title: Moonlit: Immersive Experience Design & Extended Theater Course
item.description:
Immersive Experience Devised and Produced by Students in Extended Theatre course taught by Professors Anna Henson and JD Madsen at the Center for Emerging Media Arts at the University of Nebraska, Lincoln

Overview

ROLE: Assistant Professor of Emerging Media Arts, Johnny Carson Center for Emerging Media Arts at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Moonlit was a collectively devised immersive theater production created for public audiences by students in my Extended Theater course at the Johnny Carson Center for Emerging Media Arts (University of Nebraska–Lincoln). Undergraduate EMA students and MFA Theater Design candidates collaborated to design and build an original, multi-room interactive environment integrating experience design, worldbuilding, experimental performance, scenic and projection design, sound, lighting, and emerging technologies. Emphasizing audience agency and embodied exploration, the experience invited guests to move through a narrative world rather than observe from a distance. Industry mentors from Meow Wolf contributed professional insight, and the project culminated in a ticketed public run that transformed university space into a temporary community cultural venue, demonstrating how interdisciplinary education can generate ambitious, inclusive immersive art for broad audiences.

item.title: Projection Design
item.description:
Overview

A selection of projection design work spanning Broadway, Off-Broadway, experimental theater, and international production. Projects include collaborations with directors Julie Taymor, James Walski, Mahesh Dattani, and Yin Mei Critchell, and with projection designers Peter Nigrini, Daniel Brodie, and Adam Larsen. Venues include The Public Theater and Stage 42 in New York, Steppenwolf Theater in Chicago, LaMama Experimental Theater, Barnard College, and the Ningbo Song and Dance Company in China.

item.title: Somatic Avatars: AT_REACH Research in Addiction Recovery
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Principal Investigator

Effect of a Novel Somatic Avatar Training on Distress Tolerance Among Unhoused Men Recovering from Substance Use Disorders: A Pilot Study — Journal of Technology and Behavioral Science →

This pilot study introduces somatic avatar (SA) training as a brief interoceptive intervention combining emotion-focused yoga with the creation and animation of personalized 3D avatars that visually encode participants’ bodily and emotional states. Participants design avatars to represent their felt experience during yoga, which are then animated using their recorded movements; viewing these avatars operationalizes theories of embodied cognition, vicarious learning, and the Proteus Effect by enabling distanced self-observation and rehearsal of somatic-emotional states.

item.title: Styles and Customs of the 2020s
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Producer

In this Virtual Reality (VR) experience, artists invite us to consider how a re-imagined future can shed light on our present moment.

This newly commissioned work, built by Scatter, and based on a creative brief by DIS, presents a digital dystopia inflected by rapid climate change, social unrest, and shifting global economics. Inside the VR environment, users will be transported to an ancient cave, animated by the flickering light of an age-old fire. Slowly, the cave begins to dissolve, revealing one of four scenarios from the 2020s. Over the course of 3–4 minutes, users are transported forward in time, to scenes in which humanity itself is in a state of dissolution. Space-steading billionaires, sound-canceling isolation bubbles, water crises, and killer drones clad in artisanal Tuscan leather — these scenes are all science fiction. But, like the best science fiction, they tell us more about the present than the future.

item.title: VR Home
item.description:
Overview

ROLE: Designer/Prototyper and Researcher: prototype concept development, lead development and implementation of co-design activities with research participants, user study analysis, paper co-author

This research project explores the idea of a hybrid virtual-physical home that uses virtual space to supplement an existing physical home, identifying methods for meaningful and embodied communication across distance.

Led by Principal Investigator Dr. Jessica Hammer with funding from Verizon, our research team conducted a user study that revealed the expectations and needs people have for virtual home spaces, including security, familiarity, and community. We then prototyped and playtested three virtual rooms — built for the HTC Vive with Unity 3D and Maya — and identified design features that supported feelings of home. The research also surfaces key challenges to designing home-like VR environments that can shape future work in this area.

item.title: Wake: Co-located, Co-Present Mixed Reality Experience
item.description:
Overview

Wake is a mixed reality performance and research project — a guided experience for one participant in-headset, one dancer, and one facilitator. The participant is immersed in a virtual environment and uses spoken instructions and movement to navigate the space, interact with virtual and tangible objects, and encounter a co-located, virtually present dancer who invites them into simple collaborative movement.

The experience is built in Unity 3D for the HTC Vive, Vive trackers, and an Intel RealSense Depth Camera placed at the position of the participant’s eyes in the headset. The project uses a custom algorithm to stream and render in real-time a high resolution volumetric video (synced depth + RGB feeds) of a physically and virtually co-present dancer.
